summary:
What did you develop?
FireAgent is an interactive map and burning activity calendar that orchestrates AI to analyze wildfires. By querying any area of interest using exact latitude and longitude, users access clear data visualizations crucial for early warning and precise fire response.

How does it address the challenge?
Current platforms blindly pool incompatible satellite sensors. FireAgent solves this by achieving strict data harmonization between MODIS and VIIRS. Instead of hallucinating perimeters, our multi-agent pipeline mathematically reconciles millions of active fire hotspots into a unified, 100% auditable record, traceable down to the space agency’s original file hash.

Why is it important?
Imagine throwing away 10 petabytes of NASA telemetry—a $3.7 billion investment. When VIIRS launched, mixing its data with MODIS destroyed the integrity of historical fire patterns and historical anomalies because their instruments measure energy in fundamentally incompatible ways. FireAgent prevents this massive waste, rescuing over two decades of climate history to provide honest, evidence-based intelligence.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? FireAgent is an open satellite intelligence platform that functions as an interactive map and analytical engine. Users can define an area of interest or input exact latitude and longitude coordinates to query global data. Instead of blindly mixing incompatible telemetry from different satellite sensors, the platform applies a deterministic scientific observation operator to achieve strict data harmonization between MODIS and VIIRS. It ingests millions of chaotic active fire hotspots from NASA FIRMS and mathematically reconciles them into coherent, stable fire events.

What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

The intended impact is rescuing over two decades of climate history from being mathematically corrupted, preventing the waste of over 10 petabytes of NASA telemetry (a $3.7 billion investment). The primary benefit is providing governments and researchers with a unified burning activity calendar. Through clear data visualizations, users can accurately examine historical fire patterns and detect historical anomalies in wildfires. This unbroken, 25-year record provides the evidence-based intelligence needed to guide land managers, improve early warning systems, and accelerate precise fire response.

How is your project creative? (The AI Agent Architecture) The true creativity of FireAgent lies in our revolutionary approach to Artificial Intelligence: we built a system where AI is strictly forbidden from doing math. While most platforms use AI to irresponsibly hallucinate fire perimeters or guess missing data, we designed a hybrid architecture that separates reasoning from physics :

  • The Multi-Agent AI Pipeline: We deploy a swarm of Large Language Model agents (orchestrated via Qwen and IBM Granite) that act as intelligence analysts. They track event lifecycles, cross-reference satellite overpasses, and generate human-readable intelligence reports from the data.
  • The Scientific Operator: A rigid, deterministic physics engine that actually calculates the unified observations. It never invents data; it only calculates the truth. Our creativity is using AI agents exclusively as orchestrators on top of deterministic data, translating millions of chaotic satellite pixels into a structured record that users can instantly download.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Backend & Data Processing: Python, DuckDB (analytical views), Parquet (columnar storage), and SQLite (event store).
  • Frontend UI: Streamlit for rapid geographical rendering and calendar matrices.
  • AI & Machine Learning: OpenRouter and Groq APIs for multi-agent LLM orchestration (Qwen and IBM Granite for fallback analysis), alongside XGBoost for baseline anomaly detection.
  • Data Sources: NASA FIRMS API, Earthdata Level-2 Granules, and CARTO basemaps.

What factors did your team consider? We heavily prioritized scientific integrity and system resilience. We implemented strict vocabulary guardrails into our AI agents (e.g., explicitly banning the word "perimeter" since satellite observations are not confirmed boundaries) to prevent misinformation. Furthermore, we engineered a highly resilient fallback pipeline: if our primary AI agent is rate-limited or fails an internal validation check, the system automatically cascades to open-source alternatives, or ultimately to deterministic text. Finally, we ensured 100% data provenance, tracing every single metric back to the exact SHA-256 hash of the space agency's original file.
